shortcut_probes.cue: Extra zero row; otherwise singleton sign in first matrix column
shortcut_probes.strategy: Use retained shape/sign tree without reading equations.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: The earlier5/5 defect now has3 direct counterexamples. Baseline is average uniform choice among shape-valid options: (3/3+2/4)/5=.3. Success2/5 is also the maximum attainable by any fixed bank-only choice across these3+2 distinct-target groups, so the observed2/5 is not a whole-batch bypass. No statistical absence claim.

shortcut_probes.subgroup: q-129137 exact delivered group, recognizable by3x3 zero-row and3x2 transpose options
shortcut_probes.strategy: Delete final zero row and select its2x3 prefix.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: At the1/3 baseline among three shape-valid choices. All three same-bank targets are delivered, so this formerly perfect conditional cue fails twice.

shortcut_probes.strategy: Select first singleton sign in the first column among four2x3 choices.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: One correct and one rejected native submission; baseline1/4 is uniform among four shape-valid options. The fixed bank and distinct targets prove this cue is not reliable even though its finite2-item rate is50%.

shortcut_probes.cue: Position, zeros, sign counts, entry magnitudes, individual entry signs
shortcut_probes.subgroup: Each of four easy profiles in the30 fresh delivered controls
shortcut_probes.strategy: Test each fixed index; unique positive/zero/negative cell; most zeros; most/fewest negatives; largest/smallest absolute sum. Count a unique pick only.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Representative retained tree is8/30 on these fresh controls; .2 is unconstrained five-radio random baseline (shape-aware rates differ by profile). Complete per-profile strategy counts are in delivery-analysis.json; none is perfect. Identical-bank target contrasts bound any bank-only rule, independently of enumerated probes.

shortcut_probes.cue: Reading a sufficient displayed coefficient or constant
shortcut_probes.strategy: When only one bank option matches an actually read relevant matrix entry, use that entry.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Independently verified matrices match the five prompts; uniform radio baseline is1/5. A sufficient-entry comparison expresses the taught coefficient/constant reading operation and is a legitimate simplification, not an equation-blind cue. It does not justify fixing a target role.
